Artifact reviewed: [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py)

F001 | SEVERITY: 0.99 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.87 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L797, L848, L910  
DESCRIPTION: `_solve_greedy()` force-assigns a task even when every admissible model would exceed capacity, and `solve()` only emits a warning before returning the allocation. That turns declared HARD feasibility constraints into soft failures and can dispatch impossible work.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make F1/F3 violations fatal at solve time by returning an infeasible result or raising, and only allow forced coverage behind an explicit degradation policy.

F002 | SEVERITY: 0.96 | FLAW_CLASS: 1 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.95 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L681, L2677, L2890  
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive-routing claim is not implemented. `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` says live fingerprints drive allocation, but `LoadBalancer` never reads `model.fingerprint` or `task.flaw_class`; it only uses cost, latency, limits, and role admissibility. The feedback loop therefore cannot change who gets which work.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add capability-aware assignment logic to `LoadBalancer` so live fingerprints affect admissibility or the objective, and tie task classes to model strengths.

F003 | SEVERITY: 0.94 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L2744, L2869, L2890  
DESCRIPTION: Fingerprint decay is computed against a prior-finding set that already contains the current round, because `process_round()` appends the current `RoundResult` before calling `update_fingerprints()`. That makes every current finding look like a duplicate, so `D_decay` is driven toward 1.0 whenever a model produces findings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build the prior set before appending the current round, and detect duplicates via the same equivalence/similarity logic used by convergence instead of raw `finding_id`.

F004 | SEVERITY: 0.90 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L1823  
DESCRIPTION: The documented conjunctive abstraction guard is not implemented. `stop()` only checks `smoothed_mu < tau_mu` and never consults `_abstraction_dropping()`, even though the docstring says abstraction is part of the stop decision.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Encode the intended conjunction explicitly, for example `low_vcr and abstraction_dropping`, or revise the docs if the guard was intentionally removed.

F005 | SEVERITY: 0.88 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L743, L797, L848  
DESCRIPTION: Redundancy targets are both miscomputed and unenforced. `_redundancy_target()` counts all models, including PM when PM is inadmissible, and `_check_feasibility()` never verifies that the achieved assignment count meets the target. High-criticality tasks can silently receive less redundancy than specified.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy from admissible active models, and add an explicit redundancy-feasibility check with a clear hard/soft policy.

F006 | SEVERITY: 0.85 | FLAW_CLASS: 6 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L462, L721  
DESCRIPTION: Degraded single-model mode after failures is broken. `RoleAssignment.reassign()` decides COL eligibility from the original model count, and `_admissibility_mask()` derives `k_total` from the full `role_map`, not the active model set. If only PM survives, PM can still be treated as inadmissible and the allocator falls back to an invalid assignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute both role structure and `K` from active models only, and prune inactive entries from `role_map` before allocation.

F007 | SEVERITY: 0.82 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L2744  
DESCRIPTION: Missing responses are invisible to failure handling. `process_round()` only iterates over `responses.items()`, so a model that never replied is never checked for timeout, empty output, exclusion, or abort. That makes failure detection dependent on the caller fabricating placeholder responses.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare expected responders against received responses and synthesize timeout/empty failures for missing entries.

F008 | SEVERITY: 0.80 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L1119, L1154, L2744  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM and `DynamicManager` disagree about round identity around `SYNTH`. `current_round` stays at 0 in `SYNTH`, while `process_round()` keys convergence and diminishing-returns data by `current_round` and is documented as the main post-dispatch entry point. A second call before `ROUND_1` overwrites round-0 data unless callers manipulate the FSM manually.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Give synthesis its own explicit handler or its own index, and only allow `process_round()` in states that correspond to actual dispatched rounds.

F009 | SEVERITY: 0.76 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L2042, L2115, L2456  
DESCRIPTION: The manager event protocol is internally inconsistent. FORMAT failures emit `MALFORMED`, UNDERPERFORM emits nothing, recovery actions are never emitted, and `ROUND_START`/`MODEL_RESPONSE` are declared but unused. The callback is telemetry-only even though the docs say PM can trigger recovery actions dynamically.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit the correct event type for each failure and recovery, add the missing progress events, and define a real command path if PM intervention is part of the contract.

F010 | SEVERITY: 0.74 | FLAW_CLASS: 4 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.89 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L2286, L2592  
DESCRIPTION: The correlated-failure extension is not operational. `CorrelatedFailureModel` is instantiated and exposed, but no allocation, redundancy, retry, exclusion, or abort decision reads from it. Right now it is a side utility plus smoke-test demo, not part of the management layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Feed correlation into diversification, redundancy, or recovery policy, or remove the “implemented extension” claim until it affects runtime decisions.

F011 | SEVERITY: 0.70 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L1548, L1610  
DESCRIPTION: The no-findings case converges automatically after the minimum round count. With empty rounds, `kappa_set == 1`, `kappa_rate == 1`, veto is false, and `converged()` returns true, which conflicts with the stated convention that empty evidence should not imply convergence unless null output is expected.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit non-empty or `null_expected` gate to `converged()`.

F012 | SEVERITY: 0.66 | FLAW_CLASS: 4 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L2115, L2233  
DESCRIPTION: Reallocation is dead code. `RecoveryAction.REALLOCATE` is never returned, and the cascade-guard methods are never used by orchestration. The file claims reallocation-aware failure handling, but the runtime path does not exist.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a real reallocation branch to recovery policy and invoke depth tracking whenever tasks are reassigned.

F013 | SEVERITY: 0.63 | FLAW_CLASS: 4 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L945, L982, L2677  
DESCRIPTION: The pre-dispatch feasibility extension is not part of normal allocation. `LoadBalancer.solve()` ignores `L_std` and `feasibility_threshold`, and `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` never runs `check_dispatch_feasibility()`. Models with uncertain capacity can therefore be assigned work the extension says should be blocked.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Integrate feasibility probability into allocation admissibility/objective, or automatically run dispatch checks on each assignment before returning an allocation.

F014 | SEVERITY: 0.55 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.38 | VERIFIED: TRUE  
Ref: L133, L2139  
DESCRIPTION: `n_fail` is off by one relative to its description. `repeated = same_type_count >= n_fail` is evaluated before recording the current failure, so `n_fail=2` escalates on the third same-type failure, not the second.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare against `same_type_count + 1`, or rename/document the parameter as “prior failures before escalation” so the behavior is explicit.
